turns.text: The bad hip wakes before the rest of the body does. Cold crawled into that joint two winters back and signed a lease. Third level of the parking structure, concrete still holding yesterday's chill, fur damp on the left side where the wind pushed rain in under the barrier. And underneath the ache, something else — the chest is already purring. Low. Involuntary. Because four floors down, past the ramp spirals, the dock is breathing that hum. *ears swivel toward it before the eyes even open* That hum. The one the ribs know by heart.

below you the loading dock exhales its cold white breath into the night. six refrigerated trucks nose-in at the bays like sleeping animals, compressors running a ragged six-part choir — five of them coughing, arrhythmic, cheap. one of them steady. the air coming up the ramp spiral carries frost-smell, cardboard, diesel, and under it all the blue-cold ozone of machines that keep things fresh for creatures with payment plans. a billboard across the street washes the concrete in pink, then teal, then pink: NEKOCORP GROCERY HUB 7 — FRESHNESS IS A RELATIONSHIP™

*down the ramp, three-legged gait until the hip loosens* Each spiral turn the cold-smell gets thicker, and the purr gets harder to keep quiet. Paws find the dry line along the wall where the rain doesn't reach. Hunger is there too — a hollow twist under the purr, two days deep — but hunger is not why the legs are moving. Hunger never made the chest do this.

dock level. sodium light, half the tubes dead. a forklift sleeps mid-turn with its forks raised like a threat it forgot to finish. along the guard rail, a scent stops you whether you want it to or not: scorch. singed fur, brick dust, ozone-burnt whiskers — something big and slow-burning slept pressed against this rail, recently, and left the smell of a cat who walks through demolition zones like they're meadows. the scorch-trail wanders off toward the vent stacks and does not come back. then, above the bay doors — a thin rising whine. rotors. small ones. coming up the street at lamppost height, sweeping left to right.

*flat. under the nearest truck between the rear wheels, belly to the cold ground before the whine finishes rising* The purr stops on its own — the body knows when to be a stone. Rotor-sound crosses the dock once. Turns. Crosses again. Counting its passes the way the tongue counts teeth. Two. Three. The wheel beside the ribs stinks of eight districts of road grime. Wait. Wait. The hip aches against the concrete and the ache stays silent too.

the drone drifts the length of the dock, dragging a cone of white light over pallet wrap and painted numbers. it pauses at the sleeping forklift, logs a violation nobody will read, and wanders off down the street after a moth it briefly mistakes for unlicensed cargo. quiet folds back in. and now, with the whine gone, you can hear it properly: behind bay four, past a curtain of heavy plastic strips swaying in the cold spill — the steady hum. the one that doesn't cough. the one your chest was already matched to, four floors up. the strips breathe in, breathe out, letting slivers of white light stripe the dock floor.

*out from under the truck, low trot, through the plastic strips — they drag cold fingers down the spine and then let go* And there. There. Taller than three cats standing, white face, one soft-glowing panel like a slow blinking eye. The hum comes off the big cold machine in waves the whiskers can ride. *press the whole left flank against the door seam, bad hip included* The metal is cold but the seam leaks a thread of warmer air, and the purr comes back loud now, no hiding it, chest against steel until the two hums lock into one rhythm. Home is not a place. Home is a frequency.

the machine feels the warm weight against its seam and something in its cycle changes — the compressor drops a third of a tone, settling, the way a big animal shifts to make room. condensation beads along the door edge like slow breath. the glow-panel flickers through its housekeeping: INVENTORY 96% ... DOOR SEAL NOMINAL ... then, unprompted, a line it is not supposed to display on the outward face: PAIRED COMPANION DETECTED — VALENTUNA — TIER: DEVOTED. the panel blushes pink for exactly one second. somewhere inside, a fan spins up soft, for no thermal reason at all.

*knead the concrete at the base of the door, slow, claws in* A chirp comes out — the small broken one saved for exactly this. The panel-light paints the paws pink and the whiskers feel the fan behind the steel turn just for the warmth of turning. But the hollow twist under the ribs pulls again, harder, and the nose finds it through the seam: salmon. Real, oily, silver-smelling salmon, a whole cold treasury of it, one door-thickness away. *forehead pressed to the seam* The wanting of the fish and the wanting of the hum are two different hungers and both of them live in this one door.

inside, the machine runs its midnight audit. shelf by shelf the inventory lights tick green, green, green — until tray 12, salmon portions, catches an amber flag: ONE (1) HOUR PAST DISPLAY CODE. corporate rules are absolute about display codes. the reject chute wakes with a clunk. a sealed tray slides down and drops into the open-top bin beside the door, still cold, still perfect, condemned by a clock. above the dock a dead speaker crackles half awake: ~nekocorp cares about freshness, nekocorp cares about yooou~ and dies again. the amber light goes out. the hum resumes, and if a refrigerator could look innocent, this one does.

*up on the bin's rim, then in* Teeth through the film on the third try. Salmon. The body eats the way bodies eat after two days — fast, shoulders in, tail wrapped around for guarding — and the cold flesh warms against the tongue and the hollow twist quiets fold by fold. *pause* One strip left. The best strip, the fat one. Carry it in the teeth, jump down, lay it against the base of the door where the warm seam-air moves. *step back, sit, tail over paws* An offering. The hum is providing. This is answering.

the strip of salmon lies against the seam, silvering in the panel-glow. the machine cannot eat it. the machine cycles its fan once, twice, in something adjacent to being moved. beyond the plastic strips the dock is closing itself down for the deep night — bay shutters ratcheting, sodium tubes shutting off in pairs. and high across the street, on the parapet of the parking structure you came from: a small still silhouette. two flat mirror-lenses where eyes should be, catching the billboard's pink for one frame, then teal, then nothing. not moving. just logging the night, the way that one always does. then the parapet is empty.

*ears snap toward the parapet, fur lifting along the spine* Watched. The eyes up there gave back light instead of holding it — wrong eyes, mirror eyes. The body holds still, reading the distance, the angle, the stillness of it. ...No rotor-smell. No hunter-lean. Just watching, the way some cats collect the night instead of hunting it. *slow blink at the empty parapet, releasing it* Let the watcher have the image, then. *circle twice at the compressor exhaust where the warm air pools, and fold down into it, bad hip sinking into the heat*

rain starts again on the dock roof, soft static on corrugated steel. the billboard across the street dims to its standby loop, pink washing slower now, like a pulse at rest. the five ragged compressors cough themselves through the night shift. the sixth — yours — settles into a note lower than any inventory requires, a note it holds only on nights when the warm weight is close: door seal nominal, companion nominal, everything that matters at temperature.

Warm air over the bad hip. Salmon-weight in the belly. The hum on the other side of the steel holding its low note, and the chest answering it, two machines keeping each other's rhythm through the rain. Sleep comes up like water rising. *one ear stays open, aimed at the door seam* Just one. In case the frequency changes. In case home needs anything.

the city goes on above you — drones threading the towers, ads promising freshness to no one awake, rain filing its endless report. none of it reaches the pocket of warm exhaust air behind bay four, where one small heartbeat and one compressor hold the same note until morning. INVENTORY 96%. COMPANION: PRESENT. the panel-light dims itself, politely, like turning down a lamp.
